contentTest.audience: A Madison-area homeowner (Madison, Middleton, Waunakee, Verona, Sun Prairie, the near west side) who cares how her home is furnished, values a designer's eye and Midwest makers, and would like a hand in what Patina becomes. Addressed directly about her own home under VISION-DECISIONS V21 (amends V17 beyond the homepage) and voice.md §1 (Founding Circle campaigns). She is not addressed as Patina's customer: the studio remains the customer (VISION §2, V21 'unchanged'); membership is an invitation into the building of Patina, never a sale. No shop line, no products, no prices or fees (not even 'free'), no discount, no urgency beyond the published cap of 200 [C33]. First reached through Leah's own past and current clients (VISION §2 names Middle West's active clients as the first homeowner cohort) and then Madison-area press, 1:1, never SEO strangers.
contentTest.moment: Fall in Madison: the season she looks around her own rooms and starts planning what comes next, a room she wants to finish, a piece she wants made to last. Per V21 the studio-moment check reads as the homeowner's moment, and it still has a studio behind it: Middle West Studio, Leah's, inviting its own clients to help shape what Patina brings in before the app launches. Surfaces served, in VISION's ranking: the iOS app, the studio's front door, which founding members are first through at launch [C34]; and the marketplace, the till, whose makers and styles founding members help choose [C35]. Not The Document, which stays the studio's working surface and is never shown or sold here.
contentTest.promise: The Founding Circle's own promise, as the live page states it: a place at the table. Founding members help choose which makers and styles Patina brings in [C35], hear from Kody and Leah as it takes shape [C36], are first through the door when the app launches [C34], are credited by name at launch and stay founders for good [C37], and begin with a first letter from Kody [C38]. Underneath it sits VISION §4's homeowner promise, one agreed direction with her designer, told through her own home and the people behind it, never through engagement, dashboards or a funnel.

The reader is a homeowner, but she is not Patina's customer and the batch never treats her as one: nothing is sold, nothing is priced, no product or catalog appears, and the only ask in every piece is to join the Founding Circle at patina.cloud/founding [C38], an invitation into the building of Patina. concept.name: A place at the table
concept.idea: It is fall in Madison and she is looking at her own rooms again: the living room that never got finished, the dining table she wants made to last. Patina is being built a few miles from her, by Kody and Leah at Middle West Studio [C01], around a real designer's eye and Midwest makers, and it is not open yet [C24]. The Founding Circle is her seat at that table while it is still being built: a monthly say in which makers and styles come in [C35], word from Kody and Leah as it takes shape [C36], first through the door when the app launches [C34], her name on it at launch and a founder for good [C37], beginning with a first letter from Kody [C38]. Two hundred seats [C33], open wherever she lives [C39]. Nothing to buy, nothing to shop; the one ask in every piece is to join at patina.cloud/founding. Three angles, one per social post and echoed across the print and letter pieces: the room she keeps looking at (her home, a sample held to the window with her designer); who makes it (a modern Midwest workshop, and her say in which makers come in); built in Madison, in the open (Kody and Leah, the studio where it is being made, hearing from them as it takes shape). Leah's letter speaks to her own clients in her own voice; the PR pitch gives a Madison editor the checkable facts and one ask; the poster and one-pager carry the invitation into a cafe or design shop and home from it.
concept.artDirection: Lived-in Madison-area homes in fall light: low afternoon sun through tall windows, maples turning outside, a sample or a sketch in a homeowner's hand with her designer beside her, candid and mid-conversation, faces at a natural distance and never looking into the lens. A maker's workshop that reads modern and bright: tall windows, a laptop, a CNC in the background, a white oak board against a printed drawing; no antique tools, no grime, no worn hands as the subject. A contemporary Madison design studio with its sample library, laptop and monitor, printed plans pinned. Materials up close as supporting shots (white oak, walnut, linen, a pencil sketch). Furniture only in the background, never the subject; every generated image carries the word 'Illustration' where a caption or credit would sit and is never described as a real home, client, studio or maker. Paper ground (#EDE9E4), Playfair Display headlines in sentence case, Inter body, DM Mono eyebrows for place and date lines (Madison · Fall 2026). Instagram: image owns the top two thirds, headline on paper below, text out of the outer 64 px. Pinterest: tall image, headline over a paper band at the foot. Email: letter first, from Leah, one image at most under the opening paragraph, readable with images off. One-pager: eyebrow, Playfair title, one image band, four single-column sections, CTA at the foot, print-safe. Poster: one image, one Playfair line readable from six feet, no QR-first design. Flat paper, ink and clay-beige hairlines; no gradients, badges, red/green, product screenshots or Patina mark as hero. Midjourney house style per art-direction.md §5 (--v 8.2 --style raw --s 40 --p m7507783415631638492); {{SREF}} stays unset. No coastal signifiers; Madison, Middleton, Waunakee, Verona, Sun Prairie and the near west side are the place cues.

Four sections, each a heading and ≤ 70 words: (1) the moment: fall in Madison, she is looking at her own rooms, a room to finish, a piece to be made to last, and the people behind a home like that, a real designer's eye and Midwest makers; (2) what the Founding Circle is: an invitation into the building of Patina, not a purchase; Patina's app and marketplace are pre-launch [C24]; then the five membership benefits as the live page names them, each in a line: First access, first through the door when the app launches and first to test it as it is built [C34]; Real influence, monthly questions on which makers to bring in and which styles to explore [C35]; Behind the curtain, updates from Kody and Leah as Patina takes shape [C36]; Your name at launch and Always a founder, credited by name at launch, founding-member status never expires [C37]; (3) who is building it: Kody and Leah at Middle West Studio in Madison, Wisconsin [C01]; Patina starts with studios in Madison and Milwaukee and grows outward through Leah's network [C08]; open wherever she calls home, rooted in Madison [C39]; (4) what it asks of her: join at patina.cloud/founding, where membership begins with a first letter from Kody [C38]; the circle is limited to 200 founding members [C33], stated as the cap only. One CTA at the foot: patina.cloud/founding. This is the ONE piece in the batch that may carry 'Where Time Adds Value', once, as a footer line, never a headline; every other piece omits it. Byline 'Kody and Leah', names only. Hard rules: no products, no prices or fees (not even 'free'), no discount, no fake urgency, no count of places left; never 'AI'; no Pledge; no time-saved; no Moll Drive; no claim that any studio besides Middle West uses Patina; no feature grid, no comparison table.
